title: Shipping JPEG XL in Chrome
titleZh: 在 Chrome 中传送 JPEG XL
author: AshleysBrain
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: We're excited to announce that Chrome is shipping decoding support for the JPEG XL (.jxl) image format starting from Chrome 155. JPEG XL is a next-generation image format designed to meet the needs of modern web developers and photographers. It offers 30-50% better compression than JPEG, lossless compression, built-in HDR support, lossless JPEG transcoding, and more.

In general, we recommend trying both AVIF and JPEG XL to get the best results. We expect that JPEG XL is most helpful for high-fidelity or lossless compression, especially of photographic images or in cases in which fine-grained progressive decoding is preferred.

In this post, we share why we brought JPEG XL to Chrome, how we used Rust to ensure memory safety first, the extensive performance work that makes it fast, and what the journey tells us about developer feedback and the web standards ecosystem.
Safety first: Reimplementing the decoder in Rust (jxl-rs)
summaryZh: We're excited to announce that Chrome is shipping decoding support for the JPEG XL (.jxl) image format starting from Chrome 155. JPEG XL is a next-generation image format designed to meet the needs of modern web developers and photographers. It offers 30-50% better compression than JPEG, lossless compression, built-in HDR support, lossless JPEG transcoding, and more.

comments.author: jug
comments.textRawHtml:
And soon Firefox will include it in Stable. During October it will go from Safari only to majority coverage. Eventful month!

While AVIF may have a slight edge in some cases like in fairly lossy compression, you won't really go _wrong_ with JPEG XL (unless strongly CPU constrained) and I think the strength of the format is its extreme versatility as a "be all end all image format" for some time where comparative performance depending on functionality ranges from respectable to excellent. It can work as a replacement for AVIF, PNG, JPEG, WebP, even certain TIFF required scenarios (high bit depth, multichannel, layers) depending on use cases.
comments.textZhHtml:
很快 Firefox 就会将其纳入稳定版。 10 月份，它将从仅覆盖 Safari 变为覆盖大部分地区。多事的一个月！

虽然 AVIF 在某些情况下可能有轻微的优势，例如在相当有损的压缩中，但使用 JPEG XL 并不会真正出错（除非受到强烈的 CPU 约束），而且我认为该格式的优势在于它作为“万能图像格式”的极端多功能性，在一段时间内，根据功能的比较性能范围从可观到出色。根据用例，它可以替代 AVIF、PNG、JPEG、WebP，甚至某些 TIFF 所需的场景（高位深、多通道、图层）。

children.author: kibwen
children.textRawHtml:
No, the reverse. Mozilla opposed Google's original attempt to push JPEG XL years ago, and declined to ship without an implementation that they could confidently say was safe. See https://hacks.mozilla.org/2026/08/intent-to-ship-jpeg-xl/ :

"We added experimental support for JPEG XL behind a flag back in 2021. But, at 100,000 lines of multithreaded C++, we were concerned about the attack surface this added to Firefox. So, we laid down a challenge to the JPEG XL team at Google Research: Build a safe, performant, compact, and compatible JPEG XL decoder in Rust, and we’ll ship it. That challenge was met; Google Research built jxl-rs, and it’s the core of our JPEG XL support in Firefox."

不，相反。 Mozilla 多年前就反对 G​​oogle 最初推动 JPEG XL 的尝试，并且在没有他们可以自信地说是安全的实现的情况下拒绝发布。请参阅https://hacks.mozilla.org/2026/08/intent-to-ship-jpeg-xl/：

children.author: F3nd0
children.textRawHtml:
That’s not at all how it went.

Years ago, both Chrome and Firefox had experimental support. In October 2022, Chrome suddenly announced their decision to drop it (citing dubious reasons like lack of interest or improvements over existing formats). [1] It was only later, in January 2023, that Mozilla announced their formal position of not really caring about the format. [2]

In October 2023, one of the JPEG XL devs said that the responsible team at Google was ready to write a decoder in Rust if that was the only reason holding adoption back, even offering to work on browser integration. [3] One month later, another dev confirmed that a different pre-existing decoder written in Rust was already standard-conformant. [4]

It wasn’t until September 2024, nearly a whole year later, that Mozilla changed their official position from not caring to waiting for a suitable decoder written in Rust. [5] And it was only then that jxl-rs development really picked up. [6] Only later on, Chrome decided to change their position as well, but we can only speculate on what actually changed their mind.

There was no Google shoving JPEG XL down everyone’s throat like they once did with WebP. There was no Mozilla taking a clear, principled stance from the get-go. Whether or not JPEG XL was worth it, neither of these companies has acted in a transparently fair, exemplary way. And of course the first major browser to ship JPEG XL support to users was Safari, which may well have played a role in the others’ decision-making.

  [1]: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40168998#comment85
  [2]: https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/issues/522#issuecomment-1409539985
  [3]: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/430#issuecomment-1776762287
  [4]: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/430#issuecomment-1811972676
  [5]: https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/pull/1064
  [6]: https://github.com/libjxl/jxl-rs/graphs/contributors?from=03%2F01%2F2024&to=01%2F01%2F2026
children.textZhHtml:
事情根本不是这样的。

几年前，Chrome 和 Firefox 都提供了实验性支持。 2022 年 10 月，Chrome 突然宣布决定放弃它（理由不明，例如缺乏兴趣或对现有格式进行改进）。 [1] 直到后来，即 2023 年 1 月，Mozilla 才宣布他们并不真正关心格式的正式立场。 [2]

2023 年 10 月，一位 JPEG XL 开发人员表示，如果这是阻碍采用的唯一原因，Google 的负责团队已经准备好用 Rust 编写解码器，甚至提出致力于浏览器集成。 [3] 一个月后，另一位开发人员确认用 Rust 编写的另一个现有解码器已经符合标准。 [4]

直到 2024 年 9 月，将近一年后，Mozilla 才将官方立场从不关心转变为等待用 Rust 编写的合适解码器。 [5] 直到那时，jxl-rs 的开发才真正开始起步。 [6] 直到后来，Chrome 也决定改变他们的立场，但我们只能猜测到底是什么改变了他们的想法。

Google 并没有像以前对待 WebP 那样将 JPEG XL 强行塞给每个人。 Mozilla 从一开始就没有采取明确、有原则的立场。无论 JPEG XL 是否值得，这两家公司都没有以透明、公平、模范的方式行事。当然，第一个向用户提供 JPEG XL 支持的主要浏览器是 Safari，它很可能在其他浏览器的决策中发挥了作用。

children.author: F3nd0
children.textRawHtml:
Firefox did not take very long to support AVIF (another recent image format clearly favoured by Google). Please do correct me if I’m wrong, but I’m not aware of Mozilla expressing any reluctance over AVIF’s abysmal lossless performance or other shortcomings (some of which have been addressed since), or insisting on using a memory-safe decoder like they have for JPEG XL. Why the stark difference in treatment?

We may not be able to say for certain, but Google’s massive influence is by far the most plausible explanation I can think of. And if the first step in your decision making is looking at what Google is doing, then ‘following marching orders’ is suddenly not such a bad description. (One can argue that with 3 % market share they don’t have much choice, but that’s beside the point.)
children.textZhHtml:
Firefox 很快就支持了 AVIF（另一种近期明显受到 Google 青睐的图像格式）。如果我错了，请纠正我，但我不知道 Mozilla 对 AVIF 糟糕的无损性能或其他缺点（其中一些已经得到解决）表示不愿意，或者坚持使用像 JPEG XL 那样的内存安全解码器。为什么待遇会有如此明显的差异？

我们可能无法肯定地说，但谷歌的巨大影响力是迄今为止我能想到的最合理的解释。如果你决策的第一步是看看谷歌正在做什么，那么“遵循行军命令”突然就不再是一个糟糕的描述。 （有人可能会说，凭借 3% 的市场份额，他们没有太多选择，但这不是重点。）

children.author: kibwen
children.textRawHtml: Mozilla was a founding member of the Alliance for Open Media, having sponsored Xiph to create Daala, which was later polymerized with Google's VP10 to create AV1. Mozilla has a vested interested in pushing all things related to AV1, including AVIF. That has nothing to do with Google's favor and everything to do with Mozilla's favor. Their hope was to use the existence of AVIF as leverage to give hardware vendors more incentive to provide hardware support for AV1.
children.textZhHtml: Mozilla 是开放媒体联盟的创始成员，赞助 Xiph 创建了 Daala，后来与 Google 的 VP10 聚合创建了 AV1。 Mozilla 对推动所有与 AV1 相关的事物（包括 AVIF）有着既得利益。这与 Google 的青睐无关，而与 Mozilla 的青睐有关。他们希望利用 AVIF 的存在作为杠杆，让硬件供应商更有动力为 AV1 提供硬件支持。

children.author: F3nd0
children.textRawHtml:
> Mozilla has a vested interested in pushing all things related to AV1, including AVIF.

Why? AV1 was developed as a video codec. That doesn’t imply it’s as good of an image format nor that everyone who supported its development has vested interest in making it into one. Just because someone has made a cool hammer doesn’t imply they now need to view everything as nails. (This provenance even brings some drawbacks with it, yet this time seemingly no one took a pause before tossing in yet another image format.)

> Their hope was to use the existence of AVIF as leverage to give hardware vendors more incentive to provide hardware support for AV1.

This is the first time I’m reading about this and I’m having a hard time seeing how decoding images would make for a significant incentive to provide hardware support (especially when everyone was already more or less on board with AV1 as a video codec). But I could be wrong, of course. If you can provide any links where Mozilla gives this reason for adopting AVIF or any hardware vendor gives significant consideration to decoding AVIF in hardware, it would be much appreciated.
children.textZhHtml:
> Mozilla 对推动与 AV1 相关的所有内容（包括 AVIF）有着既得利益。

为什么？ AV1 是作为视频编解码器而开发的。这并不意味着它是一种很好的图像格式，也不意味着每个支持其开发的人都有将其变成一种图像格式的既得利益。仅仅因为有人制作了一把很酷的锤子，并不意味着他们现在需要将一切视为钉子。 （这个出处甚至带来了一些缺点，但这一次似乎没有人在投入另一种图像格式之前停下来。）

>他们的希望是利用 AVIF 的存在作为杠杆，让硬件供应商有更多动力为 AV1 提供硬件支持。

这是我第一次读到这篇文章，我很难想象解码图像将如何极大地激励提供硬件支持（尤其是当每个人都已经或多或少地使用 AV1 作为视频编解码器）。但当然，我可能是错的。如果您可以提供任何链接，其中 Mozilla 给出了采用 AVIF 的原因，或者任何硬件供应商都认真考虑了在硬件中解码 AVIF，我们将不胜感激。

Again, when exactly has Google endorsed JPEG XL? When did they promise to ship it in Chrome stable? Sure, they had it in development as an experimental feature at first, but so did Firefox.

children.author: yyyk
children.textRawHtml:
* I don't deploy anything not supported in current Firefox ESR. That's June-July 2027.

* The versatility is a bit of a downside when it comes to lossless. Programs play games when it comes to formats mixing both and when may appear to be lossless isn't always thus. It would have been nicer if there was a direct way (via extension+mime) to indicate lossless is expected.

* JPEG transcoding is a very nice feature.
children.textZhHtml:
* 我没有部署当前 Firefox ESR 不支持的任何内容。那是 2027 年 6 月至 7 月。

* 在无损方面，多功能性有点不利。当涉及到混合两种格式时，程序会玩游戏，而当看起来无损时，情况并非总是如此。如果有一种直接的方式（通过扩展+mime）来指示无损是期望的，那就更好了。

* JPEG 转码是一个非常好的功能。

children.author: Broiler9437
children.textRawHtml: Quantized PNGs are a thing and those are not easily detected either. For JXL, most files compressed with Modular mode are lossless. You can detected them in the metadata
children.textZhHtml: 量化 PNG 是一种东西，但它们也不容易被检测到。对于 JXL，大多数使用模块化模式压缩的文件都是无损的。您可以在元数据中检测到它们

children.author: yyyk
children.textRawHtml:
The problem is not that a file with a lossless extension (e.g. PNG) may have actually had lossy processing.

The problem is that it's not necessarily trivial to tell programs/pipelines/transforms to act only losslessly (there's definitely no common switch; Quality 100 is in fact still lossy in some encoders/formats). In practice some programs use the extension to realize what they should be doing.
children.textZhHtml:
问题不在于具有无损扩展名的文件（例如 PNG）实际上可能进行了有损处理。

问题在于告诉程序/管道/转换仅进行无损操作并不一定是微不足道的（绝对没有通用开关；Quality 100 实际上在某些编码器/格式中仍然是有损的）。在实践中，一些程序使用扩展来实现它们应该做什么。

children.author: jjcm
children.textRawHtml:
Rollout looks solid, but I'll probably avoid deploying it to anything live til early next year at the minimum. That'll give time for browser adoption to happen.

Biggest concern I have was the same I had with AVIF a couple years ago, which is hardware acceleration on the server side. I attempted to roll out AVIF only to find out the encoding time was so long that sync calls were timing out due to queuing. It's gotten a lot better, but just know that all of these newer formats really do need more compute. It may not be worth the cost tradeoff vs webp until encoders are baked into chips.
children.textZhHtml:
部署看起来很可靠，但我可能至少会避免将其部署到明年初之前的任何活动中。这将为浏览器的采用提供时间。

我最大的担忧与几年前对 AVIF 的担忧相同，即服务器端的硬件加速。我尝试推出 AVIF，结果发现编码时间太长，同步调用因排队而超时。它已经变得更好了，但要知道所有这些新格式确实需要更多的计算。在编码器被烘焙到芯片中之前，与 webp 进行成本权衡可能不值得。

children.author: dabinat
children.textRawHtml:
I had the same problem with AVIF. My platform allows users to “scrub” through a video file they’ve uploaded by hovering over the thumbnail. To achieve this it creates a grid of 100 representative frames, up to 480px in width per frame. So the images are pretty large and take up a lot of space in JPEG format. File size is important because it reduces lag time before the thumbnail is scrubbable.

We tried AVIF and file sizes were much better but it would take multiple minutes just to generate. We also got feedback from our self-hosted customers that it was using way too many of their system resources.

So we’re now using WebP which generates in about 10 secs using much less CPU. I’m open to JPEG XL if it can improve on those metrics.
children.textZhHtml:
我在使用 AVIF 时遇到了同样的问题。我的平台允许用户通过将鼠标悬停在缩略图上来“浏览”他们上传的视频文件。为了实现这一点，它创建了一个由 100 个代表性帧组成的网格，每帧宽度最大为 480 像素。因此，JPEG 格式的图像非常大并且占用大量空间。文件大小很重要，因为它可以减少可擦洗缩略图之前的延迟时间。

我们尝试了 AVIF，文件大小要好得多，但仅生成就需要几分钟的时间。我们还从自托管客户那里得到反馈，称它使用了太多的系统资源。

因此，我们现在使用 WebP，它在大约 10 秒内生成，使用的 CPU 少得多。如果 JPEG XL 能够改进这些指标，我对它持开放态度。

children.author: caniload
children.textRawHtml: yeah this is the underrated part of the jxl pitch, encode cost. cjxl at effort ~7 is meaningfully faster than aomenc/rav1e at their high quality presets, and effort 5-6 is honestly fine for thumbnails with a small size penalty. still not hardware speed, but for user-upload pipelines the cpu bill matters as much as bytes saved. worth re-running your benchmark if it's been a while.
children.textZhHtml: 是的，这是 jxl 音调中被低估的部分，编码成本。 cjxl 的努力 ~7 比 aomenc/rav1e 在其高质量预设下要快得多，而努力 5-6 对于缩略图来说确实很好，但尺寸损失很小。仍然不是硬件速度，但对于用户上传管道来说，CPU 费用与节省的字节数一样重要。如果已经有一段时间了，值得重新运行基准测试。
